The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

📅 17 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (385 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace.
  • As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.
  • The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Sources indicate that interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

In a recent development, unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the tech giant may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the latest paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

Earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a latest dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

In a recent development, what is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big upcoming lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff.".

According to recent reports, if the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

In a recent development, there's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an upgrade there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as major a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the fresh one on Steam.

Can you free-roam after beating GTA 6?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, no matter how far you're through the main GTA 6 missions list, you are probably starting to get a sense of just how massive Leonida really is – and how stacked it is with curiosities, distractions, objectives, and side-activities.
  • I'm going to answer this question for you and, because I'm nice, I'm going to do so in the most spoiler-free way that I possibly can.
  • Sources indicate that you can continue free-roam after beating GTA 6, albeit with a few caveats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, no matter how far you're through the main GTA 6 missions list, you are probably starting to get a sense of just how massive Leonida really is – and how stacked it is with curiosities, distractions, objectives, and side-activities. So naturally you must be wondering if you can free-roam after beating GTA 6, or whether you need to pack everything in before hitting a point of no return.

I'm going to answer this question for you and, because I'm nice, I'm going to do so in the most spoiler-free way that I possibly can.

Sources indicate that you can continue free-roam after beating GTA 6, albeit with a few caveats. Because there are numerous GTA 6 endings, with a wide range of different variables and impacts for all of the characters depending on your relationship status, your criminal profile, whether you paid into family savings, and plenty more besides, Rockstar has decided that it would be far too difficult to simply drop you back into Vice City in a world in which there are no more main missions daunting your GTA 6 Index.

This means that once you've completed the main story in GTA 6, the game will drop you back to an auto-save just before the point-of-no-return. When the game does this, I recommend that you be prepared to make a new save in GTA 6 – as that auto-save won't exist forever, and can be lost if you decide to load an old save or start the campaign over from scratch.

From this point, you're free to do whatever you want to do. Your relationship status will be locked, so there's no need to worry about maintaining this if you don't want to, but you can still mess around with your Criminal Profile. You can also, at any point, restart the final mission and go through it again.

In a recent development, the GTA 6 end-game is where the world really lets you be free. You'll have loads of GTA 6 challenges to complete, which contribute to the unlocking of GTA 6 Cheats that are now available in the Progress menu. So, long story short, you can free-roam after beating GTA 6, but expect to have that final mission sitting on your menu screen for the long haul.

Recent findings suggest that when you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a latest interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

Recent findings suggest that "Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a new interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.".

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

In a recent development, in any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

  • Sources indicate that new Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATE 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a Newly introduced Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

Sources indicate that new Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

There'll be new versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

The full patch notes for Dawnwalker patch 1.2 are:.

ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A New Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Update 1.2, currently planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a New Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

According to recent reports, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions.".

Elsewhere in Enhancement 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

It has been revealed that the new game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful.".

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons presently in the works, and a wealth of newly introduced additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging newly introduced video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

In a recent development, the video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

According to recent reports, we’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

In a recent development, the introduction of naval combat will bring with it a newly introduced dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

Industry observers note that the idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being said, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just launched into early access.

To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be big or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

That's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nintendo apparently agonized over The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's emotional ending cutscene.

Ocarina of Time remake producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi - the developer who also served as game director on Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom - mentioned as much in an interview with Game Informer, explaining that he's "very, very happy" to hear that the remake's finale is having an emotional affect on some players.

"That cutscene – cutscenes in general – but that cutscene specifically is something that we, as a dev team, heavily discussed," Fujibayashi says of the game's ending. "Because of the limitations of the technology back in the day, there might have been things that we weren't able to convey fully, whether it's because of the tempo of the game… whatever it is.".

Industry observers note that almost three decades of hardware improvements and technical know-how let Nintendo realize the scene fully, as it was first intended all those years ago on the N64. "And so, when we approached this remake, we wanted to make sure that we captured that moment in the way that we wanted to express it. So that the right kinds of emotions are evoked, and that we can convey the emotion and the story that we wanted to at that moment," Fujibayashi adds.

The Zelda maestro is just "really relieved to hear" people are having strong reactions to the end of the game and its full-circle send off.

It has been revealed that the Switch 2's Ocarina of Time seems to have been welcomed with glowing reactions across the board. Nier Automata's Yoko Taro just had to pick it up, Final Fantasy Resonance lead said it was a masterclass in remakes, and the game also managed to become the best-selling US physical release of the year after just one week.

Feature: GTA 6 Made Me Want to Be a Good Guy (or Girl)

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually abiding by the traffic rules.
  • I’m playing a latest GTA game but I’m clicking L3 and R3 to focus and targeting non-vitals.
  • I’m playing a latest GTA game but I’m actually opting to defuse the situation when an NPC gets mad at me.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually abiding by the traffic rules.

I’m playing a latest GTA game but I’m clicking L3 and R3 to focus and targeting non-vitals.

I’m playing a latest GTA game but I’m actually opting to defuse the situation when an NPC gets mad at me.

The more I reflect on my time with GTA 6, the more I realise this is not the GTA I necessarily grew up with, even though the carnage is always there bubbling beneath the surface.

That’s because just like GTA Vice City and GTA San Andreas, I do have the option to go on a reckless murdering spree.

I could stock up on grenades and sticky bombs and create chaos on a highway.

I could go to a beach and mow down innocent bystanders in a scene so gruesome it’d make Jack Thompson pass out.

I think this is the most remarkable thing about GTA 6 – it’s made me play differently to past titles, even though nothing has actually changed.

In a recent development, so, why is this? Why am I choosing non-lethal as much as humanly possible, when the game allows me to go mental if I want to?

I think it’s a few reasons, personally.

Firstly, Jason and Lucia certainly aren’t saints by any stretch, but they just don’t seem like the type to go on a killing spree.

This isn’t the first GTA game to have protagonists with a slightly softer personality – GTA 4’s Niko immediately springs to mind, as does GTA 5’s Franklin.

But I think with romance being one of this game’s central themes, you really get to know these characters intimately.

It’s about the quiet moments, rubbing your partner’s feet in front of the TV.

It’s relatable – and if it’s relatable, then I think the vast, vast, vast majority of us are kind and caring to others.

Of course, this is still a video game and I racked up kills in the hundreds by the end of the campaign, but I never felt like I was doing it on purpose.

I made mistakes – I sometimes knocked cyclists clean into the air. I wouldn’t do that in real-life. But I did try to avoid these moments as much as possible here.

One other wrinkle is that the realistic graphics mean the violence is pretty visceral. It’s fascinating to think how much criticism the PS2 trilogy got at the time, when it looks like a cartoon compared to this game.

I wouldn’t say the violence necessarily deterred me from being a cold-blooded killer, but I can see how it would affect others.

And also it’s a gameplay mechanic, right?

Behaving recklessly and showing no real care for other virtual life will alter your criminal profile, and change how the world reacts to you.

I ended up with a personality trait sitting somewhere between saint and sinner, but I think that’s probably normal as you’re still going to have to punch an NPC in the mouth from time-to-time.

I’m sure there’ll be people who see the GTA series as more of an arcade game than the life sim it’s become in GTA 6, and there’ll be many who don’t like this change.

For me, I’m fascinated by how Rockstar subtly convinced me to play a GTA game like it’s not a GTA game. And I didn’t even really notice it until recently.

That’s just one of the title’s many, many achievements – and one of the reasons why it’s now the highest rated game of all time.

Recent findings suggest that have you found you’re playing GTA 6 in a less aggressive manner than past titles? Are you taking care on the road and picking the non-lethal option wherever possible? Be a bit nicer to the Leonida natives in the comments section below.

Industry observers note that if a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

First up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

Sources indicate that I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

According to recent reports, the other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only announced this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The latest season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each fresh season.

Industry observers note that you’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

According to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Industry observers note that netflix first declared a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

It has been revealed that IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Recent findings suggest that glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and says the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss.
  • You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon.
  • Sources indicate that as you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

In a recent development, tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

Sources indicate that as you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Significant Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

In a recent development, peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

According to recent reports, A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

According to recent reports, again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arthur Morgan's hat is found in GTA 6, a genuine cowboy hat that serves as a easter egg and reference to Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar's previous game and sibling franchise to Grand Theft Auto. Not just found on a hook somewhere, Arthur's Hat can actually be purchased and added to Jason and Lucia's wardrobe permanently - if you know the location of who's selling it.

According to recent reports, to get Arthur Morgan's brown leather cowboy hat for yourself in GTA 6, you need to go to a yard sale in the South of Port Gellhorn, found at the location marked above. The sale is marked by several very obvious balloons floating outside.

Once there, head to the couch at the end, where you'll see a guitar case and a hat resting on it. That's Arthur Morgan's hat, though GTA 6 calls it a "Genuine Cowboy Hat" in Brown Leather. You can buy it from the owner, though the price seems to vary. When I bought it, it was $35, though some online have reported it being cheaper than that, suggesting the cost might be randomised.

Once purchased, the hat will be in your wardrobe and clothing inventory permanently! For a little easter egg has the seller mention that she has no idea where the hat came from: perhaps she's a descendant of John Marston, the last canonical owner of that hat?

Industry observers note that this region will be a lot easier to access once you reach chapter 2. To see how far you are from that point if you haven't reached it yet, check out our GTA 6 Mission list. Or for more in-game easter eggs, check out where to find the GTA 6 Paul Walker car.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store.
  • In a recent development, the main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next major revision, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive manufacturer’s debut on Valve’s platform.

In a recent development, the main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two fresh arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

According to recent reports, the first fresh Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

It has been revealed that by using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver substantial Physical burst damage.

Recent findings suggest that the higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

In a recent development, re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the latest Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Industry observers note that throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

Industry observers note that if you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a upcoming Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

Sources indicate that "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics.".

Sources indicate that "Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "Newly introduced features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

According to recent reports, according to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

Industry observers note that for info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 launched on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and debuted either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," noted Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, states it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Industry observers note that other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

Industry observers note that it comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently revealed it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ received a new GTA 6-themed secret run this week, alongside the evergreen indie hit's PS5, Switch 2 and Xbox console ports, but players were quick to sniff out music generated with AI.
  • According to recent reports, player concerns were quickly confirmed by the game's original lead designer and Mewgenics co-creator Edmund McMillen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer Nicalis has removed AI-generated music that appeared in a fresh upgrade for roguelike darling The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+.

In a recent development, the Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ received a new GTA 6-themed secret run this week, alongside the evergreen indie hit's PS5, Switch 2 and Xbox console ports, but players were quick to sniff out music generated with AI. Redditor ShweetsStuff found that the mode's new tracks were "100% generated with Suno (AI) (with proof)," by looking through "metadata included in the files shipped with the game.".

According to recent reports, player concerns were quickly confirmed by the game's original lead designer and Mewgenics co-creator Edmund McMillen. "Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned," he tweeted.

It didn't take long for Nicalis to scrub the music in question from the game, either. Just yesterday, the studio pushed out a new revision that removed "generated music files" on PC, alongside bug fixes and netcode improvements. The update has also been "submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo and Sony ASAP." There's no word on how exactly the genAI tracks slipped into the game.

Nicalis is also "fixing compatibility that was inadvertently broken for the mod community (thanks for making cool stuff!)" Look forward to more in future updates, then.

According to recent reports, the controversy had a huge knock on effect to The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s Steam rating, as well. It now has an Overwhelmingly Negative rating on the platform, with just 8% of recent reviews logged as positive. "It's impressive that you can add nothing but crossplay in two years and somehow multiply the amount of bugs by three despite trying to fix those," one user review reads.

After Slay the Spire 2 update led to negative Steam review spike, Mewgenics lead jokes releasing balance patches for popular games is "the scariest thing a human can experience".

According to recent reports, kaan freelances for various websites including Rock Paper Shotgun, Eurogamer, and this one, Gamesradar. He particularly enjoys writing about spooky indies, throwback RPGs, and anything that's vaguely silly. Also has an English Literature and Film Studies degree that he'll soon forget.

Industry observers note that harada, who worked as a producer on both versions of the game, wanted the fighting / dark-type Pokémon 'Pangoro' from Generation VI. In a recent development, there were many discussions before finalising the roster, and a lot of it came down to the gameplay and systems in place, along with The Pokémon Firm's own requests. Here's what Harada had to say about this (via EventHubs):.

Harada: "We had thorough discussions before finalizing the roster. There were Pokémon that the development team wanted to include from a gameplay and systems perspective, and of course, The Pokémon Company also had its own requests for which Pokémon they wanted to see in the game.".

After the release of Pokken Tournament DX for Switch, the final roster included the following Pokémon (this included some Switch-exclusive and DLC Pokémon).

It has been revealed that as you can see, the final roster is an interesting mix. Harada, who is now the CEO and game director of SNK's VS Studio, added how he was just personally happy at the time to see the lineup include Pikachu and Gengar.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that "Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is presently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

It has been revealed that "Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson mentioned in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

According to recent reports, "We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile said in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

It has been revealed that inXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

Sources indicate that according to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three new projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

It’s not yet clear what form the fresh game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources noted it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially introduces a new Vegas game.

Rainbow Six Vegas rolled out in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two latest Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are at the moment no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

  • Sources indicate that wyman wants you to locate old wrecked Transgressors hidden across the open world.
  • Sources indicate that located in the north Port Gellhorn area, next to the Kolt & Associate's Stash House robbery spot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you purchased the Ultimate Edition, you're no doubt wondering where to find all of the Transgressor parts in GTA 6. As soon as you've completed the Thrillbillies objective from the GTA 6 Missions in Chapter 2, you'll unlock Wyman's Wyman’s Car Collection under the exploration tab.

Sources indicate that wyman wants you to locate old wrecked Transgressors hidden across the open world. If you locate all three of the GTA 6 Transgressor Locations, he'll restore the car for a small fee and then it'll be yours to keep or scrap for cash. The three parts are situated in the Port Gellhorn area, so below I'm going to tell you how to find all of the parts so you can get your very own '67 Transgressor in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that located in the north Port Gellhorn area, next to the Kolt & Associate's Stash House robbery spot. Directly opposite the gang hideout there's a small house. Head down the right-side of the building towards the back of the driveway, which is where you'll find the first Transgressor wreck inside of an open garage. Walk up the building, hold Up on the D-pad to open the WAiNK app and scan it with R1/RB to send the photo over to Wyatt.

In a recent development, if you head slightly north from Sarena's Bargain Store, you'll be able to head off-road and into a trailer park. Right in the middle of this area, surrounded by pigs and garbage, is where you'll find the second Transgressor wreck. As before, you'll need to scan it with the WAiNK app to get Wyman to come collect.

In a recent development, to the south of Port Gellhorn is the Dirt Merchants mod shop. Head right over there and look for a dirt road to the right of the location. Head all the way down this path until you reach some fence, which is where you'll find the third and final Transgressor part for Wyman. Scan it and you're good to go.

Once all three car wrecks have been scanned and sent across to Wyman, he'll contact you to say that it's going to take a few days for something to be assembled and restored. After around two in-game days, Wyman will request $1500 for labour costs via the BuckMe app. Once this is paid, wait another day or so and the car will be ready for collection from Wyman's Auto Shop.

You can register the Transgressor as a personal vehicle in GTA 6 for $100 or sell it for $15,000. The good news is that if you want to keep the vehicle but don't have any garage space, the Transgressor will be returned to his scrapyard if it isn't saved for later collection.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I think we all knew it was going to be significant, but this big? Rockstar has unveiled that GTA 6 sold a staggering 32.5 million copies during its preload period, setting a “new record across all platforms”.

That number is likely higher by now, because the press release’s wording implies it’s not counting launch day sales into the above total, which are guaranteed to be plentiful. (It’s only going to keep rising through Thanksgiving and Christmas, too.).

Rockstar says the game generated a frankly mind-boggling $3.79 billion on day one, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. Estimates claim it cost about $1 billion to make.

It’s also eager to point out that the title is now the highest-rated game of all-time as well, with its near-perfect 99 Metacritic score nudging the N64 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time aside.

“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of GTA 6. We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”.

The dev didn’t specify how sales were split between systems, but the expectation is the PS5 version sold best, with some estimates pegging it at around 75% of the total.

Sony was the primary marketing partner of the game, and promoted the fact it “plays best on PS5” (even though testing reveals it’s broadly identical to the Xbox Series X version on base hardware).

This is just the beginning for GTA 6, of course, with no word on Rockstar’s aims for the next iteration of GTA Online just yet. The game is also expected to launch on PC in 2027 as well.

If you’re one of the 32.5 million people playing, don’t forget to check out our GTA 6 guide for tons of information on the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a upcoming Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next revision has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

It has been revealed that luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its newly introduced Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

Recent findings suggest that if you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter rapidly is a fresh Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”.

Sources indicate that and if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

According to recent reports, her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Industry observers note that lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Manufacturer, is the second fresh character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Sources indicate that through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

It has been revealed that prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

According to recent reports, nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a fresh limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

Sources indicate that you’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a fresh sports festival for you to take part in.

Sources indicate that one upcoming gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

You've most likely already completed the GTA 6 Transgressor locations quest if you've gotten this far, but regardless I'm now going to help you hunt for a gorgeous '70s Riata.

There are three wrecked Riatas that you need to scan with the WAiNK app, and sadly these are a little more spread out across Leonida than the Transgressor locations. So jump in your favorite ride and get ready to do a little driving to unlock the off-road 4x4 for personal use.

You'll need to head down to Southwind to wrap this mission up. To the east of Zero Mile station, on the middle prong of the trident when you're looking at the map, is where you'll find the third Riata location. It's underneath a brown house near the coastline. Send that back across to Wyman, and you're almost there.

Recent findings suggest that once you've found all three Riata locations in GTA 6 and sent the details over to Wyman, he'll contact you to say that he's ready to get to work – but it's going to take a few days. Kill some time by doing other activities, and eventually Wyman will text you to request $1500 for costs to restore the vehicle. Once you've Bucked him the cash, wait another day or so and you'll get a notification that the Riata is ready for collection from Wyman's scrapyard.

Recent findings suggest that you can register the '70s Riata as a personal vehicle in GTA 6 for $100 or sell it for $15,000. If you want to keep it but don't have the garage space, the Riata will be returned to his scrapyard if it isn't saved for later collection by either Jason or Lucia.

Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

📅 15 May 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (720 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years.
  • Sources indicate that the free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts.
  • The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving newly introduced content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

Sources indicate that the free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

Sources indicate that the message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a upcoming automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large revision for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very rapidly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

In a recent development, it’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without latest content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

To find out how this dating system works, here’s a Mystic Messenger primer that explains it all. Once you’ve wrapped your head around it, you’ll no doubt want to pick the correct answers for every guest, and this guide will help you nail every one.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

Industry observers note that the BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Industry observers note that kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the organization contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

According to recent reports, earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two rapidly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are four Mamba GT locations in GTA 6, part of the Wyman Classic Car quest that is exclusive to owners of the Ultimate Edition. By now you should have found all the Transgressor locations and Riata locations in GTA 6, and be well on your way to getting a very sweet Mamba GT sports car restored.

It has been revealed that like every other GTA 6 mission you've had to do for Wyman so far, there are Mamba GT wrecks spread out all across Leonida. You need to find all of these, scan them with the WAiNK app, and then Wyman will get to work on the restoration. This time, you're going to have to go to some pretty far out locations, so I'd recommend having a fast car or a bike to help you get around off-road.

The first Mamba GT location is north of the Leonida State Penitentiary, and east of the Gellhorn area more generally. There's a large house that's kind of in the middle of nowhere which, once location, will be letting the Mamba GT rust in its garage. Open the door up, scan the vehicle, and you're good to move on.

Recent findings suggest that the second Mamba GT location is in the Leonard County area, on a backroad in Ambrosia just north of the Pay 'n' Spray. Head around the back of the building from the main road and you're looking for a closed white garage door, next to a big orange building. Break into here and you'll be able to scan the wreck with the WAiNK app.

In a recent development, the third Mamba GT location is a pain to get to, so I'd recommend having a bike to get across some uneven terrain. Located north of Frogswater, the Mamba GT wreck is by a small lake in the middle of the racing park. On your bike, head across to the destination and look for the Mamba GT sat in the body of water close to the embankment.

The fourth and final Mamba GT location is way up in the north, near Bonanza and just south of the Saint Attaway Islands. There's an old collapsed wooden bridge, and you'll find the Mamba GT at the bottom of it in the wreckage. Here's the good news: You don't need to climb down there. Just pull out your phone and scan the vehicle with the WAiNK app.

Sources indicate that once you've found all four Mamba GT locations in GTA 6 and sent the details over to Wyman, he'll contact you to say that he's ready to restore the classic car. Kill some time by doing other activities, and eventually Wyman will text you to request $1500 for costs. Back him the cash directly, and it won't be long before you get a notification that the Mamba GT is ready for collection from Wyman's scrapyard.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game.
  • In a latest interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope.
  • Of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

In a latest interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

Recent findings suggest that then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated rolls out, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

In a recent development, that version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, presently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Sources indicate that steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

According to recent reports, game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

It has been revealed that forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales.
  • All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they unveiled a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".
